title: MS60001: Structure Property Relations In Materials
text:
Syllabus
Syllabus mentioned in ERP

Pre-requisites: None
Introduction : Types of materials from structure to property.
Crystal Structures : Seven systems and fourteen lattices; lattice direction and
planes. Understanding amorphous materials and polymers. Crystal Imperfections :
Point, line and planar defects. Mass transport:
Diffusion in Solids : Mechanisms; Fick’s laws; factors-affecting diffusion
inmetals; ceramics and semiconductors; atom mobilities, temperature and
impurity dependence of diffusion, various diffusion processes. Heat Transport:
conduction, convection, radiation. Momentum transport: viscosity, measuring
viscosity, rheology, etc.
Phase Diagrams : Phase rule; isomorphous, eutectic, peretectic, eutectoid etc.
Binary phase diagrams (Pb-Sr, Al-Si, Ge-Si, Au-Si etc), microstructure and its
effect on properties. Phase diagram of materials. Understanding polymer-solvent
interactions, polymer-polymer blends, etc in the light of theremodynamics.
Nucleation and Growth : Homogeneous and heterogeneous nucleation kinetics;
growth and overall transformation kinetics. Kinetics of polymerization
Deformation Mechanism and Mechanical Properties of Materials : Plastic
deformation of single crystals and polycrystals; strengthening mechanisms;
recovery-recrystallization-grain growth; tensile, impact, fatigue and creep of
metals and alloys; deformation behavior of ceramics and polymers; mechanical
testing methods
Quantum mechanical approach to structure of materials : Energy bands in solids;
electrical conductivity; extrinsic and intrinsic semiconductors; carrier
concentration; work function. Carrier transport mechanism : Scattering and
drift of electrons and holes; diffusion and drift of carriers; Hall effect.
Materials for use in electronic devices : Polymers, ceramics, semiconductors
and metals – their structure and properties; insulators; superconductors;
dielectric, ferroelectric, memory and magnetic materials. Case studies.
Selection of Engineering Materials : Common engineering materials including
metals and alloys, polymers, ceramics, composites, electronic materials and
their selection procedures.
